My research activities cover different aspects of
animal genetics, genomics and computational biology,
combining methodological development with applications
to specific biological questions.

The following sections describe the main research
areas and their scientific context.

## Genomics & Molecular Phenotypes {#genomics-molecular-phenotypes}

This research area investigates the genetic
architecture of molecular and intermediate
phenotypes in animal populations, with particular
emphasis on pigs.

Genome-wide association studies are combined with
high-throughput metabolomic profiles, haematological
parameters and clinical-biochemical measurements
to identify genomic regions associated with
phenotypic variability.

These analyses contribute to the characterization
of genetic factors affecting metabolic traits
and to the interpretation of their relationships
with biological pathways and complex phenotypes.

## Metabolomics, Phenomics & Machine Learning {#metabolomics-phenomics-machine-learning}

This research area focuses on the characterization
of phenotypic variability through high-throughput
molecular measurements.

Metabolomic profiling is used to investigate
differences between animal populations, sexes
and physiological conditions, as well as to
identify potential biomarkers associated with
production and functional traits.

Computational and statistical approaches,
including machine learning, are explored to
analyse complex phenotypic datasets and
investigate relationships between molecular
profiles and animal phenotypes.

## Genomics of Complex & Production Traits {#genomics-complex-production-traits}

Genome-wide association studies and sequencing
approaches are applied to investigate the genetic
architecture of complex traits in livestock
and aquaculture species.

Research activities include the identification
of genomic regions and candidate genes associated
with production, morphological and quality traits.

These studies contribute to understanding the
genetic determinants of economically relevant
phenotypes and other characteristics of
domesticated animal populations.

## Population Genomics & Biodiversity {#population-genomics-biodiversity}

Population genomic approaches are used to
characterize genetic diversity, population
structure and evolutionary processes in
domesticated animal populations.

Research activities include the analysis of
genome-wide markers, whole-genome sequencing
data, runs of homozygosity and signatures
of selection.

These approaches provide information on
population history, adaptation, inbreeding
and the genomic characteristics of local
and commercial breeds, supporting the
characterization of animal genetic resources.

## Environmental DNA, Metagenomics & One Health {#environmental-dna-metagenomics-one-health}

This research area explores the information
contained in environmental and unconventional
DNA sources.

Shotgun metagenomics and DNA metabarcoding
approaches are applied to characterize
biodiversity and environmental signatures,
including those recovered from honey.

Additional activities investigate viral
sequences in animal genomic datasets and
the use of DNA-based approaches for food
authentication and molecular traceability.

These applications connect animal genomics
with environmental monitoring, biodiversity
research and One Health questions.

## Bioinformatics, Systems Biology & Genome Interpretation {#bioinformatics-systems-biology}

This research area covers the development
and evaluation of computational methods
for the analysis and interpretation of
biological data.

Previous work includes network-based
functional enrichment, analysis of molecular
interaction networks and computational
approaches to genome interpretation.

Research activities also include the
assessment of methods for genetic variant
prioritization and the application of
statistical and machine learning approaches
to complex biological problems.

These methodological activities provide
a computational background for research
across different biological systems.
